problem: PointNav agents trained in Habitat are compared under inconsistent, under-examined training recipes (visual encoder, advantage normalization, PPO hyper-parameters), and compute cost is ignored, so it is unclear what actually drives sample and compute efficiency.
motivation: PointNav with GPS+Compass is a widely used test-bed whose findings transfer to other navigation tasks. Simulation cost is compute, not intrinsic to samples, so compute efficiency should matter as much as sample efficiency. Seemingly minor design choices may be responsible for large performance gaps.
key_idea: A large controlled study (>50,000 GPU-hours) of PointNav training under a 75M-sample budget and a 1-GPU-day budget shows that ResNet18, no batch-wise advantage normalization, and larger PPO mini-batches give large consistent gains.
insight: Larger mini-batches (hyper-parameter set 2: 2 mini-batches, clip 0.2) improve both compute and sample efficiency; the rollout-length/NumSim sweep shows monotonic gains with more steps per update, and NumSim=2 underperforms. Batch-wise advantage normalization never helps SimpleCNN, gives no significant gain for ResNet18, and causes spurious performance collapses; a std-clipped/EMA variant fixes the early harm but not the instability. Under a compute budget, ResNet18 wins for RGB and RGB-D, while SimpleCNN wins for Depth-only because it collects more samples.
method: Task/agent setup: Habitat PointNav with RGB/Depth/RGB-D plus GPS+Compass. Visual encoder (SimpleCNN or ResNet18 modified per DD-PPO: half channels, 2x2 AvgPool, GroupNorm, conv+flatten to 2048-d) feeds a 1-layer GRU policy with goal embedding [r,cos θ,sin θ] and previous-action embedding.
Training: PPO with GAE (γ=0.99, τ=0.95), rollout 128, 6 simulators, LR 2.5e-4 with linear decay of LR and clip to 1/3, reward is 2.5-10x success plus -Δgeodesic minus 0.01 slack penalty.

Controlled grid: 240 agents over {RGB, Depth, RGB-D} x {SimpleCNN, ResNet18} x {Gibson, MP3D} x {norm adv vs none} x {Set 1 (clip 0.1, 6 mini-batches) vs Set 2 (clip 0.2, 2 mini-batches)}, 5 seeds each.
Compute-budget protocol: fix 1 GPU-day and convert to sample counts from measured throughput (ResNet18 8-10M, SimpleCNN 14-16M samples on a 2080Ti).
Systems improvements: double-buffered/alternating-GPU sampler (about 20% more samples) plus 10-15% other speedups, and texture-compressed MP3D meshes so training fits on a single 12GB GPU.
Batch-size analysis: sweep NumSim in {2,4,6} x RolloutLength in {32..128} with NumMiniBatch=2 for RGB ResNet18 on MP3D at 40M steps.
Normalization diagnosis: test std clipping (σ=max(σ,1)) and EMA of mean/variance for advantage normalization.

setting.backbone: SimpleCNN or ResNet18 (modified, GroupNorm) + 1-layer GRU, PPO (trained from scratch)
setting.model_size: ResNet18 and 3-layer SimpleCNN, encoder outputs 2048-d; policy is a 1-layer GRU
setting.training_data: Habitat Gibson (72 train scenes) and Matterport3D (61 train scenes), 75M frames of RL experience (or 1 GPU-day, about 8-16M samples); no extra data
setting.observation: 256x256 egocentric RGB, Depth or RGB-D plus GPS+Compass
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 10°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time beyond the GPS+Compass sensor that defines the task

numbers_note: Each paper table has 24 settings per budget; only the best/representative rows are listed. Best-case Gibson depth SimpleCNN Set 2 no-norm-adv at 75M is SR 93.1 / SPL 84.4 (Table 1 row 12). All results are on validation scenes only, mean of 5 runs.
results: Under a 75M-sample budget, RGB-D agents improve over the Habitat baselines by 8 SPL on Gibson and 20 SPL on Matterport3D. Under 1 GPU-day, they improve by 19 SPL on Gibson and 35 SPL on Matterport3D. ResNet18 helps in nearly all cases except Depth under a compute budget, larger mini-batches help everywhere, and normalized advantage is harmful or unstable.
limitations: Only PointNav with GPS+Compass on Gibson and MP3D validation scenes; the authors only expect the findings to transfer to other tasks.

Compute-budget results depend on hardware, simulator and software versions, so exact reproducibility is hard; PPO epochs (2 vs 4) were not ablated and the causes of the normalized-advantage instability remain unexplained.
